response:
Diagnosis after generation 7: the archive's frontier moved for the first time in three generations, and it moved on the **financing configuration**, not the conditioner. Rescue Equity (MIN of equity issued and debt repaid) delivered alpha -3.3% with t -3.28, the largest magnitude and the most reliable t in the entire archive, despite a modest FMB slope (-1.40); by contrast every conditioner variant on the plain net-issuance leg keeps landing at -2.0% to -2.5%. The lesson is that *simultaneous opposing capital flows* — money coming in through one channel while going out through another — identify a firm state that net flows mathematically erase, and that state is where the intangible interaction bites hardest. Two other gen-7 results discipline this batch: Shareholder-Cash-In-Minus-Research-Added produced the archive's second-best FMB (-4.25) with a weak alpha (t -1.60), the familiar signature of an unbounded asset-scaled measure whose deciles are not homogeneous; and Proceeds-Verified-as-Deployed failed with the wrong sign, showing that visible deployment does not rescue issuers, so deployment auditing is closed. With one generation left after this, I devote three slots to systematically mapping the opposing-flow family, one to a new deal-churn conditioner, one to repairing the strongest-FMB measure's portfolio side, and one to the only working long pole.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Equity Raised While Dividends Are Maintained
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(sstk, dvc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(RATIO(xrd, TS_MAX(xrd, 5)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that sells new shares in the same year it pays cash dividends is recycling shareholders' own money at a transaction cost, and when its research has also fallen below its historical peak the dividend is being defended at the expense of the innovation program that justifies its valuation.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The rescue-equity result shows that simultaneous opposing flows carry information that net measures destroy, and issuing-while-paying-dividends is the second natural configuration in that family — economically distinct from equity-for-debt-repayment because the counterparty is the shareholder rather than the lender, making it a governance and capital-allocation failure rather than creditor pressure. MIN of two non-negative, identically asset-scaled flows keeps the conjunction well defined, and the retreat-from-peak conditioner is the firm-relative state that produced the strongest FMB slope among conditioners on this configuration.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Issue-and-Repurchase Churn at Research Firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(RATIO(xrd, TS_MAX(xrd, 5)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Simultaneous large issuance and large repurchase is not financing at all — it is compensation-driven share creation being masked by offsetting buybacks; at a firm whose research has retreated from its own peak, this churn signals that cash is being routed to employees and optics rather than to the innovation program.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is the third configuration in the opposing-flow family and the one most completely invisible to every archived signal, since sstk and prstkc cancel exactly in the net-issuance leg used by a dozen prior tests, meaning the information is orthogonal by construction rather than merely economically distinct. Together with Signal 1 and the archived rescue-equity result, the three MIN configurations map whether the effect is about lenders, shareholders or employees as the true recipients of the raise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Rescue Equity at an Acquisition-Built Firm
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(sstk, dltr), at), 2), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), TS_SUM(xrd, 5)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Equity raised to repay debt is most damaging at a firm whose intangible base was purchased rather than built, because the leverage being repaid was originally incurred to buy other people's ideas and the collateral behind it cannot be liquidated without destroying the business.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Rescue-equity financing produced the archive's largest alpha (-3.3%, t -3.28) but its weakest cross-sectional slope (-1.40), and the diagnosis is its conditioner — a static R&D-to-sales level that mostly sorts industries — whereas the purchased-intangible-share conditioner is a bounded, persistent firm characteristic that independently produced FMB -2.77 with alpha -2.0%. Pairing the strongest configuration with the conditioner that carries cross-sectional power directly targets the one metric where the best portfolio signal is deficient.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Issuance Amid Purchased-Intangible Churn
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ABS(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1)), MA(xrd, 3)), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Large movement in purchased intangibles in either direction — big acquisitions or big write-offs — relative to the firm's own research budget marks a deal-driven rather than organic innovation strategy; equity raised by such firms funds a serial dealmaking process whose track record already includes reversals.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive tested goodwill *additions* (alpha -2.5%) but never the magnitude of goodwill movement, and using ABS turns a directional flow into an activity measure so that impairment years — the revelation of failed prior deals — enter the short leg alongside acquisition years instead of being pushed to the long leg where they economically do not belong. Scaling by the firm's own research budget keeps the comparison a strategy-composition measure inside the R&D-reporter universe where portfolio alpha has consistently survived.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Net Shareholder Funding Per Year of Research
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sstk, prstkc), DELTA(xrd, 1)), MA(xrd, 3)), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Expressing the gap between money taken from shareholders and dollars added to research in units of the firm's own annual research budget states how many years of research the unexplained financing could have funded, which is the economically comparable scale across a biotech and a diversified manufacturer.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The asset-scaled version of this gap produced the archive's second-strongest FMB slope (-4.25) but an unreliable alpha (t -1.60), and the pattern across the archive is unambiguous: unbounded asset-scaled measures win on cross-sectional slopes while bounded, industry-ranked ratios win in portfolios, so re-denominating in research years and industry-ranking is the specific repair the diagnosis calls for. It keeps the marginal financing-versus-research economics unchanged while making the extreme deciles homogeneous in funding-need terms rather than in balance-sheet size.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Cash Returned Through a Sustained Research Build
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(MIN(RATIO(prstkc, at), RATIO(SUB(xrd, LAG(xrd, 3)), at)), 2)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm returning cash while its research budget stands materially above where it was three years ago has demonstrated a durable ability to fund innovation internally and still have surplus; a single year's research increase can be an accounting artifact, but a three-year build cannot.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The one-year version is the only long-pole signal that has ever worked here (alpha +2.2%, t +2.06), but its raw spread Sharpe was essentially zero, which is what one expects when a noisy annual difference randomizes portfolio membership; replacing DELTA(xrd,1) with the three-year research build should raise the persistence of the long leg and convert factor-adjusted alpha into a more robust spread. Both arguments remain identically asset-scaled dollar flows, so the conjunction retains its meaning and the short leg remains firms cutting research in dollars.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Equity Raised While Dividends Are Maintained---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a single-argument substitution (dltr→dvc) into the archived "Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm" template with an identical conditioner, and because sstk is small for most firms (option exercises) MIN(sstk,dvc) will usually collapse to sstk within the dividend-payer subsample, making the signal largely a re-expression of the well-known equity-issuance anomaly conditioned on dividend status.

---CRITIQUE Issue-and-Repurchase Churn at Research Firms---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated orthogonality claim is false — MIN(sstk,prstkc) is strongly correlated with the levels of both flows, not with their difference — and since the measure mechanically selects large, cash-rich repurchasers (a group associated with *positive* abnormal returns), the natural direction of the expression works against the negative expected sign.

---CRITIQUE Rescue Equity at an Acquisition-Built Firm---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible diagnosis-driven recombination that pairs the archive's strongest portfolio configuration with its most cross-sectionally powerful conditioner, though the reasoning misattributes the archived rescue-equity conditioner (retreat-from-peak, not static R&D/sales) and the result may simply interpolate between two already-tested signals rather than add new information.

---CRITIQUE Issuance Amid Purchased-Intangible Churn---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Replacing signed goodwill change with its absolute magnitude is a substantive, well-motivated construct change (impairment years join acquisition years in the short leg rather than the long leg) rather than a cosmetic tweak, but the gain over the archived signed-goodwill version is likely modest since large positive goodwill changes dominate the right tail either way.

---CRITIQUE Net Shareholder Funding Per Year of Research---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the archived "External Funding Intensity of the Research Program" (IND_RANK of net external financing over MA(xrd,3), fmb −4.09, alpha −1.7%) with the debt legs dropped and a Δxrd term added, so it is a re-scaling recombination of two existing archive members that will be highly collinear with both rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Cash Returned Through a Sustained Research Build---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Changing DELTA(xrd,1) to a three-year difference in the archived "Buybacks Alongside Research Expansion" is a horizon parameter tweak, not a substantively different mechanism, and it also mechanically raises the signal's exposure to firm size and growth persistence, which risks a spurious apparent improvement in the long leg.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Share of the Research Budget Covered by Outside Money
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(ADD(dltis, sstk), xrd), MA(xrd, 3)), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically bounded question is what fraction of this year's research program could have been paid for out of money raised from outside investors; a program essentially fully covered by external funds is a program that continues only while capital markets stay open, whereas one covered marginally is substantially self-financed.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Capping the external inflow at the size of the research budget converts the archive's unbounded funding-per-research multiple — whose extreme deciles are dominated by a handful of enormous raises — into a coverage share in roughly the unit interval, which is exactly the outlier problem behind that signal's strong FMB slope but modest alpha. Using gross inflows rather than net flows also means the measure does not cancel against repayments, so it is a different object from the archived net-external-finance ratio rather than a dividend-for-debt substitution into an existing template.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Debt Retired While Research Expands
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(MIN(RATIO(dltr, at), RATIO(DELTA(xrd, 1), at)), 2)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm paying down lenders in the same year it adds dollars to its research budget is generating enough internal cash to satisfy creditors and expand innovation simultaneously; that joint act, made to the creditor rather than the shareholder, is a hard signal of a self-financing intangible franchise.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the churn construction — whose selection on large cash-rich repurchasers indeed fought its stated negative sign — with the creditor-side counterpart of the archive's only working long pole, which asks whether the productive-pole result is about surplus cash generation in general or specifically about equity-market signalling through buybacks. Both arguments are non-negative, identically asset-scaled dollar flows, and the bottom leg is firms cutting research in dollars, so both extremes remain economically identified.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Issuance as Total Soft-Capital Spending Retreats
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), TS_MAX(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible investment is not only research: for consumer and services firms the brand budget plays the identical role, so the informative state is retreat from the firm's own peak in total soft-capital spending, research plus advertising, and equity raised during such a retreat funds a franchise the firm has itself stopped supporting.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Advertising is the one intangible variable in the resource menu this archive has never used, and treating an unreported line as zero spending is the economically correct convention when the other line is reported, so the conditioner extends the retreat mechanism to brand-driven firms and should widen the R&D-reporter universe that has constrained every result to about 5% coverage. It is a change in the definition of intangible capital rather than a re-scaling of an existing measure, and it directly tests whether the mechanism is about research specifically or about soft capital generally.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cash Returned With Research and Margin Both Building
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(MIN(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), MIN(RATIO(DELTA(xrd, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(sale, cogs), 1), at))), 2)
HYPOTHESIS: The fully productive state requires three things at once: cash genuinely returned to shareholders on a net basis, a research budget being expanded, and gross profit rising to validate that the intangible investment is working; a firm satisfying all three is self-financing an innovation program whose output is already visible.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Rather than lengthening the horizon of the archived long-pole signal — a parameter change that would mostly load on size and growth persistence — this adds an independent output-verification leg, gross profit growth, so that research expansions unaccompanied by any realized margin improvement no longer qualify. The nested MIN keeps all three arguments as identically asset-scaled dollar flows, and netting issuance out of the repurchase leg removes firms whose buybacks merely offset option-related issuance, which was the main contamination in the one-year version.
